sources.FSIS: USDA FSIS, Keeping Food Safe During an Emergency

recipes.title: Tuna on crackers
steps: Open the can and pour off the oil (keep it — add it to other food for calories).
Put tuna on the crackers and eat.
Eat leftover tuna within 2 hours. Without a fridge, don't keep it.

recipes.title: Peanut butter crackers
steps: Spread peanut butter on crackers.
Peanut butter is high in calories and keeps a long time. Keep the lid tight.
Check first that nobody has a peanut allergy.

recipes.title: Crushed dry noodles
steps: Crush the noodles inside the bag.
Use only a little seasoning. Salty food makes you need more water.
When water is short, skip the seasoning.

recipes.title: Tuna noodles (fuel-saving)
recipes.ingredients: 1 pack noodles · 1 can tuna · 500 ml water
steps: Bring 500 ml of water to a boil with the lid on. A lid saves fuel.
Add noodles and half the seasoning, boil 2 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Add the tuna, cover and leave 3 minutes — the remaining heat finishes cooking.
Drink the broth too — it gives water and calories.

recipes.title: Soaked rice porridge
steps: Soak the rice in water for at least 2 hours. Soaking saves a lot of fuel.
Put the soaked rice and water in a pot, cover and bring to a boil.
Stir on low heat for 5 minutes, turn off, cover and leave 10 minutes.
A pinch of salt makes it good for diarrhoea or dehydration too.

recipes.title: Canned food as is
steps: Most canned food is already cooked and can be eaten without heating.
To heat it, always open the can first and move the food to a pot, or stand the open can in hot water.
The liquid in the can has nutrients and water too.
